configuration: configure.py -nr_radiation --prob=rad_linearwave --coord=cartesian --flux=hllc; 16 decks (nrrad_wave_r1_n32, nrrad_wave_r1_n64, nrrad_wave_r2_n32, ...) at the upstream settings (32 and 64 (upstream also 128 and 256) cells, t = 0.774 to 0.982, one crossing time per regime); graded: the final state of every meshblock of each deck as a full-precision tab file
observable: gas primitives and radiation moments of every cell of the 16 wave runs, eight regimes at 32 and 64 cells (amplitude 1e-6)
default_vs_upstream: 32 and 64 cells of the upstream 32/64/128/256 series; SAB_NX1_SCALE=4 restores the full series
variant: the adiabatic index gamma of every deck (it fixes the initial internal energy) multiplied by (1 + 1e-15), a few ulps; it changes the initial internal energy and hence the round-off path of the whole run without changing the physics, so the two files differ and their distance measures the floor of the policy
altbuild: the same pinned source built with configure.py -debug (Athena++'s same-compiler -O0 -g debug build) and all other configure switches unchanged, running ic/nominal: a build a correct candidate could plausibly be, with no change of source or deck

evidence.floor_how: measured by selfcheck on 2026-09-08: run.sh altbuild (configure.py -debug: Athena++'s same-compiler -O0 -g debug build, with all other configure switches and the nominal inputs unchanged) against run.sh nominal, graded with the check's own validate.py: bit-identical graded output

altbuild.what: configure.py -debug: Athena++'s same-compiler -O0 -g debug build, with all other configure switches and the nominal inputs unchanged

warrant: The graded observable is the gas primitives and radiation moments of every cell of every run of the series of 16 runs (32 files) at the upstream end time, written by the pinned code at full double precision and compared value by value under an absolute bound of 1e-11 with no relative term. Physical: the wave amplitude is 1e-6 and at 32 and 64 cells the truncation error is already a few per cent of it, so the graded final state carries the numerics of the scheme directly; upstream's own criterion is that the L1 error of the 256-cell run stay below about 1e-9 and fall faster than 0.55 per doubling. A wrong Riemann flux, a wrong angular quadrature weight, a dropped radiation source term or a lower-order reconstruction changes the graded state by 1e-9 or more at these resolutions, which is orders of magnitude above a bound of 1e-11, and it does so in eight different optical-depth regimes at once, where the upstream convergence-order criterion would see nothing. Achievable: nothing in the explicit path stops short of convergence - the gas temperature is the closed-form root of the quartic in `src/utils/fourth_polynomial_root.cpp` and the angular transport is an explicit flux update - so two legitimate builds differ only by floating-point round-off, amplified by the cancellation at lines 43 and 44 of that file (`pow(0.5 + delta1, 1/3) - pow(-0.5 + delta1, 1/3)`, special-cased only above BIG_NUMBER at line 39) and then carried through the whole run. Measured: the -O3 and -O2 builds are bit-identical on all 32 graded files (floor 0), and the 1e-15 perturbation of the adiabatic index grows to a largest absolute difference of 4.3e-14, in regime 5 at 64 cells. The bound of 1e-11, shared with the other three linear-wave checks whose spreads lie between 6.9e-15 and 4.3e-14, sits 231 times above it. Absolute rather than relative because one graded file spans identically zero velocities and fluxes alongside radiation pressures of order 100, so a relative bound would be vacuous on the zeros and would track the largest component rather than the noise. Finalized on 2026-09-02: the calibration selfcheck on the x86 worker, in the oracle image on the declared 8 cpus and 4 GB, recorded an in-container nominal-versus-variant spread of 4.33e-14, equal to the floor-run preview to every digit, and the bound was set from it.
